title: Blowing up minimal intersections of a weakly normal crossings family
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], (Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), and let $B$ be a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of nowhere dense closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that every scheme-theoretic intersection indexed by a nonempty subset $J\subseteq I$ $Y_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}Y_j$ is regular and has normal crossings with $B$: etale locally its ideal is generated by a subset of a regular system of parameters in which $B$ is the product of distinct parameters. Let $C$ be the union of the nonempty inclusion-minimal members among these intersections. Then the members of this union are pairwise disjoint, $C$ is regular and has normal crossings with $B$, and for $p:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_C X\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] the scheme $X'$ is regular, the exceptional divisor is regular, and $B'=(p^{-1}(B\cup C))_{\rm red}$ is strict normal crossings with its divisorial fs log structure log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. If $Y_i'$ denotes strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], then $\bigcap_{j\in J}Y_j'$ is the strict transform of $Y_J$; all these intersections are regular and have normal crossings with $B'$. The total transform ideal of $Y_J$ is the product of its strict-transform ideal and the Cartier ideal of the union of exceptional components whose images are contained in $Y_J$.

Iterating this operation on the strict transforms terminates after at most $|I|$ steps if the intersection family is closed under intersection and has at most $|I|$ distinct members. In general the number of steps is at most the maximal number of members in a strict chain of distinct nonempty intersections; this maximum is zero when there are no nonempty intersections. The bound need not be attained when intersections are disconnected. Every original $Y_J$ then has empty strict transform and invertible total-transform ideal. The construction commutes with isomorphisms preserving the family, including permutations of $I$. At each stage the operation stops if no nonempty intersection remains; in particular the empty family produces the tower of length zero. All assertions involving $Y_J$ refer to nonempty index subsets $J$.

source.place: VIII Proposition 4.2.8, Lemma 4.2.9, Proposition 4.2.11, printed pp.120--122; VI 1.7 for the divisorial log structure on a regular SNC pair.

proof.text: Deduplicate the finite collection of nonempty $Y_J$. For two distinct minimal members $V,W$, the intersection $V\cap W$ is another intersection. If nonempty, minimality forces it to equal both $V$ and $W$, a contradiction. Thus their scheme-theoretic intersections are empty. Their union $C$ is consequently a disjoint union of regular closed subschemes. Locally at $C$ only one of these subschemes occurs, so the assumed normal-crossings parameters for that member are also parameters for $C$. For any intersection $T=Y_J$ and minimal $V$, the same argument shows $V\cap T$ is either empty or $V$ (scheme-theoretically). Thus near $V$ either $T$ is absent or $V\subseteq T$.

All centers have finite-type ideals since $X$ is Noetherian. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], the blowup $X'$ is Noetherian. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] it is unchanged away from $C$; strict transforms there are ordinary pullbacks by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-restrict]. We may compute near $C$ after the etale neighborhoods in the hypothesis and localization at their points: etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and blowups have the canonical flat base change of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. The closure defining strict transform commutes with these flat changes: apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to the schematically dense open part of its closure [def-nagata-strict-transform]; its pullback remains dense in the pulled-back closed subscheme. The open parts are quasi-compact and quasi-separated here because all schemes involved are Noetherian.

source.place: VIII Lemma 4.2.9, locality of the chart computation

proof.text: Fix a minimal $V$ and a nonempty intersection $T$ containing it. In the local ring $R$ of the preceding neighborhood, their ideals $P\subseteq Q$ have regular quotients and separately have normal crossings with the boundary. By [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion] the ideal of $B$ in $R$ is $(b_1\cdots b_r)$ for distinct members $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of a regular system of parameters (a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ remains one in the etale local ring $R$, since $R$ is flat and unramified over it). In each of the two parameter systems given by the hypothesis for $T$ and for $V$, the boundary is a product of distinct parameters $s_j$; by [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b) the primes minimal over the boundary ideal are exactly the $(b_i)$ and also exactly the $(s_j)$, and equal principal primes in the domain $R$ have generators differing by a unit. So both systems contain all $b_i$ up to units, which is the hypothesis of the next lemma. Apply [lem-per-boundary-regular-flag-parameters] to obtain $P=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$, $Q=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$ and boundary a product of selected $t_i$. Here $l\ge1$ since the center is nowhere dense. The chart with denominator $a=t_i$, $i\le l$, is $A_i=R[u_j:j\le l,j\ne i]/(t_j-a u_j)$. Apply [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart] with auxiliary boundary $V(t_1\cdots t_d)$ and the selected original boundary as $H$: its center condition is satisfied even if the original boundary is empty. In particular $A_i$ is regular and the reduced inverse image of $B\cup V$ consists of the exceptional hyperplane and the surviving original boundary hyperplanes. The quotient and local-parameter assertions of [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients] apply to every subset of these coordinates.

On that chart, if $i\le m$, the extended ideal of $T$ contains $a$, so the part of $T$ off the exceptional divisor is empty and its strict transform is empty. Its total ideal is $(a)$, since $a$ is one of its generators and all other $t_j$ for $j\le m$ are multiples of $a$. If $i>m$, the total ideal is $a(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ and the strict-transform ideal is $(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$. Indeed the quotient by the latter ideal has $a$ as a regular parameter wherever it vanishes, by [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients]; hence it has no $a$-power torsion. The closure of the localization away from $a$ therefore has exactly this ideal [def-nagata-strict-transform]. These formulas also cover $m=l$, where every strict-transform chart is empty, and $m=0$. Thus every surviving strict transform of $T$ is regular and has normal crossings with the displayed new boundary. This computation is made separately for each $T$; no simultaneous-coordinate assertion for the entire weak family is assumed.

The preceding equations hold on actual etale neighborhoods of each point of $X'$: the finitely many parameters and ideal equalities in the local ring extend after shrinking the neighborhood. Use [lem-trf-etale-regular-intersection-descent] with the empty labelled family to descend regularity of $X'$, of each strict transform $T^{\mathrm{st}}$, and of the exceptional divisor separately; no positive-codimension claim is taken from this application. The original boundary has finitely many irreducible components by [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. A nonempty strict transform of one such component is irreducible, since it is the closure of its dense open part; if that open part is empty the transform is empty. Distinct surviving components remain distinct on the complement of the center. Apply [lem-trf-labelled-coordinate-boundary-globalization] to their strict transforms and to $E=p^{-1}C$. Its local labelled hyperplanes, regular coordinate intersections, Noetherian ambient scheme and reducedness hypotheses are supplied by the charts over $C$. At a point of $X'\setminus E\cong X\setminus C$ they are supplied by [lem-sfb-snc-boundary-parameter-criterion] for the original $B$, which there equals the reduced pullback of $B\cup C$: its local ideal is $(t_1\cdots t_r)$ for part of a regular system of parameters, each surviving component is one of these hyperplanes, and coordinate intersections are regular of the expected codimension by [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b). It gives regular $E$ and a strict normal crossings boundary $B'=E\cup B^{\mathrm{st}}$. Finally [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart] gives the required fs divisorial log regular structure on $(X',B')$.

To prove compatibility with intersections it is enough to prove the binary equality $T^{\mathrm{st}}\cap S^{\mathrm{st}}=(T\cap S)^{\mathrm{st}}$ for two original intersections. It holds off $C$. Near a minimal $V$, either $T$ or $S$ is absent, or $V\subseteq T\cap S$ by step 1. In the latter case their local ideals $P,Q$ and the ideal $K$ of $V$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-per-clean-pair-subflag-parameters]: all four quotients are regular by the weak-family assumption. Choose the coordinates provided there, with $K=(t_1,\ldots,t_l)$ and $P,Q$ generated by subsets $A,B$ of these parameters. On the chart with denominator $t_i$, if $i\in A\cup B$, at least one of the two strict transforms and the strict transform of their intersection are empty. If $i\notin A\cup B$, the strict-transform ideals are respectively $(u_a:a\in A)$, $(u_b:b\in B)$ and $(u_c:c\in A\cup B)$, by the saturation calculation of step 4 and [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients]. Their sum is exactly the third ideal. Induct on the size of the index subset to obtain $\bigcap_{j\in J}Y_j'=Y_J^{\mathrm{st}}$.

For fixed $J$, the minimal centers which meet $Y_J$ are exactly those contained in it, by step 1. Over these centers, step 4 says $\mathcal I_{Y_J}\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I_{Y_J^{\mathrm{st}}}\mathcal I_E$; over every other center and away from the center it says $\mathcal I_{Y_J}\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I_{Y_J^{\mathrm{st}}}$. Therefore these local equalities glue to the asserted product with the Cartier ideal of the exceptional components whose images lie in $Y_J$. These components form an open and closed union in $E$: the centers are disjoint and each is either contained in $Y_J$ or disjoint from it. Regularity and the Cartier property of this exceptional union follow from the labelled boundary statement in step 5. The intersection equality of step 6 and the regularity/normal crossings of step 4 prove that the new family has exactly the same weak-boundary property. Each strict transform is still nowhere dense: its open part off $E$ is nowhere dense there, and the coordinate equations in step 4 show that it contains no component along $E$.

Repeat the one-stage construction just proved. Define the rank of a distinct nonempty original intersection $T$ to be the maximum number of members of a strict chain ending at $T$ in the finite intersection poset. We prove by induction on $r$ that every intersection of rank at most $r$ has empty strict transform after $r$ stages. The claim is trivial for $r=0$. Suppose all proper sub-intersections of $T$ have disappeared after $r-1$ stages. If a current nonempty intersection $S'$ is contained in $T'$, step 6 identifies $S'$ with the transform of $S\cap T$. If $S\cap T$ is properly contained in $T$, the induction hypothesis makes it empty, a contradiction. Otherwise $S\cap T=T$, so $S'=T'$. Thus any nonempty $T'$ of rank $r$ is minimal in the current family and is the center of that stage; its next strict transform is empty (step 4). The maximum rank bounds termination. There are at most $2^{|I|}-1$ nonempty indexed intersections, and any strict chain has length at most $|I|$ by successively dropping indices. In particular the bound requested for an intersection-closed family with at most $|I|$ distinct members holds. Disconnected strata can disappear early, so equality with the global poset height is not asserted.

Track every original ideal along this induction. Initially $\mathcal I_{Y_J}=\mathcal I_{Y_J}\mathcal O_X$. If at stage $n$ its total ideal is $\mathcal I_{Y_{n,J}}\mathcal L_{J,n}$ with $\mathcal L_{J,n}$ an effective Cartier ideal, step 7 factors the pullback of the first factor as the next strict-transform ideal times the Cartier ideal of the newly selected exceptional components. The pullback of $\mathcal L_{J,n}$ is effective Cartier by [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup]. Multiplying these locally principal non-zero-divisor ideals gives the next Cartier factor. At termination the strict transform is empty, whose ideal is the unit ideal, so the total-transform ideal is invertible. This also treats an originally empty $Y_J$ and a center of codimension one.

source.place: VIII Proposition 4.2.11, induction on the Cartier factor

proof.text: An isomorphism of $X$ preserving the finite indexed family, possibly by permuting its indices, preserves its scheme-theoretic intersections, equality and inclusion, hence the union of the distinct minimal nonempty members. It identifies the center ideal and all its powers, and therefore identifies the graded Rees algebras. Relative Proj sends that graded equivalence to a blowup isomorphism by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. It also preserves the open complement and its scheme-theoretic closure, so preserves each strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Repeat this argument at every stage. Composing isomorphisms gives the same graded maps and the same closure identifications, so the tower comparison respects composition. If the family, or its collection of nonempty intersections, is empty the stopping rule returns the identity tower of length zero.
